channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Secom: Lula vetou anistia a caminhoneiros que participaram de manifestações golpistas em 2022
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva vetoed amnesty for truckers who participated in post-2022 election coup attempts, as announced by Secom. The measure aims to prevent unequal treatment of those who attacked democracy, and is part of the Freight Provisional Measure.

item.title: Lula defende Marcola em reunião com aliados: 'Quem nunca pediu empréstimo para um amigo?'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended his former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Ribeiro Santana, known as Marcola, during a meeting with allies from PSOL and Rede at the Palácio da Alvorada, stating, 'Who here has never asked a friend for a loan?' and emphasizing that Marcola has made his banking and fiscal records available to justice. The case involves suspected transfers from Roberta Luchsinger, a businesswoman under investigation in the INSS scandal, with whom Marcola admits having a personal loan and having paid R$ 249 thousand. Marcola stepped down from coordinating Lula’s campaign to focus on his defense, after serving a similar role in the 2022 campaign.

item.title: Flávio diz que teve duas filhas para cuidarem dele na velhice: 'vou ter quem vai tomar conta de mim'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated he had two daughters specifically to care for him in old age, framing it as recognition of women's unpaid care work in childcare, housework, and elder support. He announced federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar as his vice-presidential running mate, emphasizing Gaspar's background in public security, while attempting to appeal to female voters, who make up 52.8% of the electorate. Although he had considered women like Tereza Cristina and Daniella Marques for the ticket, they were blocked by party neutrality, yet still voiced support for his candidacy at the event.

item.title: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Renan Santos ao g1 e à GloboNews
item.description: Renan Santos, the Missão party's presidential candidate, was interviewed by g1 and GloboNews on August 5, claiming that 80% of youths in Febem who committed crimes lacked a male figure, citing a 2007 FGV study. The Fato ou Fake fact-check found that while the study notes paternal absence as a relevant factor in crime, it does not state that 80% of Febem inmates lacked a father figure or that this factor outweighs the Gini Index; the claim was deemed inaccurate and partially false.

item.title: MP do Frete: Lula veta anistia a caminhoneiros que bloquearam rodovias
item.description: President Lula signed into law the Freight MP, which establishes permanent rules for road freight transport oversight, but vetoed provisions granting amnesty to truckers involved in post-2022 election roadblocks and altering weight inspection rules. The veto preserves existing sanctions, ensures equal treatment, and upholds ANTT’s authority and legal certainty, according to the government.

item.title: Lulinha vive em condições precárias na Espanha, diz vice do PT
item.description: PT national vice-president Washington Quaquá stated that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, lives in precarious conditions in Spain, denying allegations of illicit enrichment due to being President Lula's son. He defended the presumption of innocence amid PF investigations into influence peddling and denied wrongdoing regarding funds received by Marcola, Lula's former chief of staff, claiming they were verifiable loans.

item.title: Empresária amiga de Lulinha pagou boletos para ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula
item.description: The Federal Police identified that businesswoman Roberta Luschinger paid bills for Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, former chief of staff to Lula known as Marcola, in the second half of 2024. Marcola admitted receiving the payments as a personal loan and confirmed paying R$249,000 to Roberta, a friend of the president's son Lulinha, but did not clarify if this was the total amount received. The episode caused embarrassment at the Planalto Palace, prompting Marcola to step down from coordinating Lula's re-election campaign, with allies demanding transparency to prevent damage to the government's image amid corruption suspicions.

item.title: Lula sanciona piso do frete e barra anistia a caminhoneiros
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed into law a national minimum freight rate for cargo transportation, with adjustments tied to operational costs. However, he vetoed a provision granting amnesty to truckers who blocked roads in 2022 following Jair Bolsonaro’s electoral defeat.

item.title: Lula tem encontro com Alcolumbre, em gesto de aproximação três meses após rejeição de Messias
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) on Tuesday evening, following three months of estrangement after the rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF. The meeting signals a rapprochement between the Executive and Legislative branches, responding to allies’ calls to restore institutional relations. The encounter comes three months after the rupture caused by the rejection of Messias’ nomination to the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: GO: convenção confirma Daniel Vilela candidato à reeleição ao governo
item.description: The MDB party convention in Goiás confirmed current governor Daniel Vilela as the candidate for re-election in the October 2026 elections, backed by 12 parties and 227 of Goiás’ 246 mayors. The coalition includes MDB, PSD, Republicanos, Podemos, Avante, Mobiliza, Agir, Democrata, and party federations, aiming to secure approximately five of the ten minutes of electoral propaganda allocated by the TSE. The campaign emphasizes administrative continuity, with polls showing Vilela leading rivals such as Perillo.

item.title: Brasil não pretende retaliar EUA em caso de embaixadora
item.description: The Brazilian government decided not to retaliate against the U.S. for revoking the visa of Ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti, despite Lula calling the move irresponsible and thoughtless. The government views the action as symbolic and not affecting Viotti’s duties, but warns of a stronger response if diplomats face further affronts. Lula stated he will not receive any new ambassadors until after the elections, protesting the U.S. delay in appointing Daniel Perez as ambassador to Brazil.

item.title: Programas sociais perdem tração e acendem alerta na campanha de Lula
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows that President Lula's social programs are losing traction among voters, triggering an alert at the Planalto Palace 60 days ahead of the 2026 elections. The decline in support for these programs, designed to win electoral backing, indicates erosion in public perception of the government's social policies.

item.title: Embaixador argentino no Brasil deve voltar a Buenos Aires após crise
item.description: Argentina's ambassador to Brazil, Guillermo Daniel Raimondi, is expected to return to Buenos Aires after Brazil downgraded diplomatic relations with Argentina to the level of chargé d'affaires in response to President Javier Milei's repeated attacks on Lula. Milei has called Lula a 'thief' and 'corrupt' without evidence, referencing the Lava Jato operation. In reciprocity, Brazil's ambassador to Argentina, Júlio Bitelli, remains in Brazil while relations remain at a reduced level.

item.title: Copom volta a reduzir Selic, a 14%, para conter a inflação
item.description: The Copom cut the Selic rate to 14% for the fourth consecutive time, aiming to curb inflation. The decision comes two months ahead of the October elections, in which President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) is seeking re-election.

item.title: Girão celebra escolha de Flávio por Gaspar como vice
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) praised the selection of federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) as the vice-presidential running mate on Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) ticket, calling him a man of integrity, courage, and a strong representative of Brazil's conservative right.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula deixa equipe de campanha após revelação de repasses de investigada pela PF
item.description: Former chief of staff to President Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, requested to step down from the campaign team after the Federal Police identified financial transfers from a woman under investigation. His departure was voluntary and comes amid growing scrutiny over potential links between the campaign and individuals involved in criminal investigations. The move aims to safeguard the integrity of Lula's 2026 re-election bid.

item.title: O recado que Galípolo enviou a Lula no comunicado do Copom sobre a queda dos juros
item.description: The Central Bank, through the Copom led by Gabriel Galípolo, sent an explicit message to President Lula, warning that populist stimulus policies boosting demand — especially consumption — are pressuring inflation and undermining monetary policy effectiveness. The statement indicates that without increased productive capacity, the BC cannot continue cutting rates and warns that the current environment demands serenity and caution, implying the BC will not serve as an electoral ally for Lula in October.

item.title: Lei garante frete mínimo no transporte de cargas; saiba o que muda
item.description: The law signed by President Lula establishes the Transport Operation Identifier Code (CIOT) as a mandatory requirement for truck trips to begin, ensuring payment of the minimum freight floor for drivers. The system blocks irregular freight contracts at the hiring stage and integrates with the Electronic Fiscal Documents Manifest, enabling automatic, large-scale monitoring by ANTT to combat illegal trade and enforce minimum freight payments.

item.title: Augusto Cury anuncia Júlio Delgado como vice na disputa presidencial
item.description: Augusto Cury, the Avante party's presidential candidate, announced former federal deputy Júlio Delgado as his running mate for the 2026 elections. The announcement was made in a document titled 'Letter to the Nation', where Cury praised Delgado's career and proposed, if elected, to reform Brazil's political system, including shifting to a semi-presidentialist regime, limiting Supreme Court justices' terms, and reducing the number of justices. Cury currently has 3% of voting intentions according to a PoderData/Aya survey from July.

item.title: PGR inicia inspeção dos códigos-fonte dos sistemas das Eleições 2026
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office (PGR) began inspecting the source code of the electoral systems to be used in the 2026 General Elections, as part of the TSE's Democratic Transparency Cycle. PGR technicians are examining the electronic voting machine architecture, data capture modules, and software for transmission and tabulation of results, with work expected to conclude by February 13. The TSE emphasized that the initiative enhances transparency and invites societal contributions to improve the electoral system.

item.title: Vereadora do PSOL tenta tornar Neymar 'persona non grata' em Belém após tumulto com o Remo: 'Desrespeito com a Amazônia'
item.description: Belém city councilwoman Marinor Brito (PSOL) sought to declare Neymar 'persona non grata' following alleged verbal abuse toward Paraense athletes during Santos' Copa do Brasil match against Remo. The motion was blocked by the municipal chamber’s directing board, which refused to schedule a vote, a move Brito condemned as undermining democratic process. She argued Neymar’s conduct disrespected the Amazon and local players, framing it as more than mere sports rivalry.

item.title: Patrimônio da vereadora Zoe Martínez triplica em 2 anos
item.description: The net worth of councilwoman Zoe Martínez (PL), a federal deputy candidate, tripled from R$646,360.78 in 2024 to R$2,108,170.56 in 2026, according to Electoral Justice data. The R$1.46 million increase is primarily in financial investments such as FIDC, long-term funds, and real estate funds. Martínez did not respond to requests for comment from Poder360 before the article's publication.

item.title: Lula é o único candidato à Presidência apoiado por outros partidos
item.description: Lula is the only presidential candidate in 2026 with a multi-party ticket, formally backed by the Brazil of Hope Federation, PSB, PDT, and the Psol-Rede Federation, with Geraldo Alckmin as his running mate. This coalition grants him the largest share of radio and TV time due to the combined federal deputy bench of allied parties. All other 11 tickets are single-party, and Flávio Bolsonaro is expected to receive the second-largest share of electoral broadcast time.

item.title: ‘Quem aqui nunca pediu empréstimo para um amigo?’, pergunta Lula em defesa de Marcola
item.description: In a meeting with PSOL and Rede leaders, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended his former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Ribeiro Santana (Marcola), after Marcola left the campaign coordination due to suspicions of receiving funds from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger. Lula likened the loan to a favor between friends and criticized the right for using unproven corruption allegations to topple governments, referencing Vargas and Kubitschek. While stressing that no one in his own son Lulinha under investigation and insists that those who erred must pay.

item.title: Frei Orlando terá nome inscrito no Livro dos Heróis e Heroínas da Pátria
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.483/26, inscribing the name of Frei Orlando in the Book of Heroes and Heroines of the Fatherland. Frei Orlando, patron of the Army's Religious Assistance Service, died in 1945 at age 32 while providing religious assistance to soldiers on the Italian front, struck by an accidental gunshot. The measure honors his sacrifice and exceptional dedication to the nation.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que teve filhas para cuidar dele na velhice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated he had two daughters specifically to have someone to care for him in old age, emphasizing the traditional role of women in family caregiving and linking it to the 'care economy,' estimating that unpaid women’s labor equals 8.5% of GDP. The remarks were made during a PL event formalizing Alfredo Gaspar as vice-presidential candidate, amid campaign efforts to gain female voter support, following the rejection of Senator Tereza Cristina’s vice-presidential nomination due to the PP’s decision to remain neutral.

item.title: PGR arquiva pedido contra Gaspar para apurar desvio em emendas
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) archived the investigation request against federal deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), running mate of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 Senate race, over alleged irregularities in 'Pix' parliamentary amendments. Although the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) had flagged 'problems' in the use of these funds, the PGR determined there was insufficient evidence to proceed with the inquiry.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro elige a un diputado de bajo perfil como candidato a vicepresidente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has chosen former prosecutor Alfredo Gaspar as his vice-presidential running mate for the October elections, ending weeks of speculation. The selection aims to revive an anti-corruption message, given Gaspar’s low-profile background and experience in the Public Prosecutor’s Office.

item.title: Brasil enfrenta dupla crise diplomática sem horizonte de fim
item.description: Brazil is facing a dual diplomatic crisis with the United States and Argentina, characterized by visa revocations, ambassador expulsions, and allegations of electoral interference. The Brazilian government accuses both nations of attempting to influence the 2026 presidential campaign, citing the U.S. conditioning of agrément on political concessions and Argentine President Javier Milei’s repeated attacks on Brazilian institutions and his involvement in the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que, com Alfredo Gaspar de vice, ‘não compensará fazer impeachment’ de Flávio
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro stated that with Alfredo Gaspar as Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate, pursuing an impeachment would not be worthwhile, praising Gaspar’s selection as 'serene' and 'well-conducted'. He highlighted Gaspar’s role as rapporteur of the INSS CPMI and echoed PL allies’ concern that choosing a vice with strong Centrão ties could risk impeachment, as seen in Jair Bolsonaro’s picks of Mourão and Braga Netto.

item.title: Moraes autoriza profissional da Claro a fazer reparos na internet de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes authorized a Claro technician to enter Jair Bolsonaro's residence in Brasília to perform internet repairs, granting the defense's request. The authorization requires 48-hour advance notice with date, time, and technician identification, and mandates that unrelated electronic devices be held by security personnel.

item.title: Visto revogado expõe falência da política externa de Lula, diz deputado
item.description: Deputy Luiz Philippe de Orleans e Bragança (PL-SP) criticized the U.S. decision to revoke the visa of Brazil’s ambassador to Washington, Maria Luiza Viotti, calling it evidence of the 'bankruptcy' of Lula’s foreign policy. He attributed the move to the ideological direction of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which he claims undermines Brazil’s historic alliance with the U.S., deepens international isolation, and harms the economy through U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. The lawmaker urged a shift in foreign policy to restore ties with traditional partners and regain Brazil’s global standing.

item.title: Augusto Cury anuncia ex-deputado federal Júlio Delgado como vice na chapa presidencial do Avante
item.description: Augusto Cury, the Presidential candidate from Avante, announced former federal deputy Júlio Delgado as his running mate. He praised Delgado’s exemplary parliamentary career and commitment to public ethics, while proposing reforms such as shifting to a semi-presidential system, modifying the Supreme Federal Court, and creating a 'superminister' for Foreign Affairs.

item.title: PT e PSOL ficam com suplências de 'ministráveis' Marina e Tebet ao Senado em SP
item.description: PT and PSOL secured the first alternate positions in the Senate candidacies of Simone Tebet (PSB) and Marina Silva (Rede) in São Paulo. Laio Morais (PT) became Tebet's first alternate, while Djalma Nery (PSOL) took Marina's first alternate seat. PDT claimed the second alternate spots in both tickets, sparking internal dissent over being sidelined in the majoritarian slate.

item.title: Banco Central corta Selic pela 4ª vez seguida, para 14%, e deixa próximos passos em aberto
item.description: The Central Bank cut the Selic rate for the fourth consecutive time, lowering it from 14.25% to 14% per year, marking a gradual monetary easing cycle that has totaled one percentage point since March. The decision was unanimous but left future steps open, citing heightened uncertainty from the Middle East war, Brazil's 2026 elections, and inflation risks, despite recent improvements in inflation and activity indicators.

item.title: Lula sanciona nova lei do piso do frete
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a new law establishing the need for a minimum floor for road freight transport, without specifying a numerical value, leaving its definition to collective bargaining agreements. The law benefits truckers, transport companies, and digital platforms, and retains the pardon for fines related to road blockades after the 2022 elections. Lula stressed that the measure ensures no employer can pay less than the agreed floor, promoting dignified treatment for workers in the sector.

item.title: Por unanimidade, TRE-SP mantém inelegibilidade de Pablo Marçal
item.description: The São Paulo Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) unanimously upheld Pablo Marçal's ineligibility until 2032, confirming his conviction for improper use of social media and a R$420,000 fine. The decision can be appealed to the TSE, and the convictions remain subject to reversal. Marçal, affiliated with União Brasil, aims to run for federal deputy if he overturns the ruling, and currently polls at 9% in voter intention surveys.

item.title: Mauro Vieira rebate Argentina e nega motivação ideológica em crise diplomática
item.description: Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira denied that the downgrading of diplomatic relations with Argentina was ideologically motivated, stating it was a response to insults by President Javier Milei against President Lula and Minister Alexandre de Moraes. He emphasized that relations should be based on respect and national interest, and that ideology is secondary. The Argentine foreign ministry, however, accused Brazil of acting on ideological grounds and isolating itself regionally.

item.title: Confira a pauta de julgamentos do TSE desta quinta-feira (6)
item.description: The TSE will judge nine processes this Thursday (6) at 10h, including an appeal on a voter's conviction for disrupting election work in Nova Lima (MG) in 2022, analysis of a triple list for a judge vacancy in TRE-MG, two administrative processes and an electoral consultation by the PT. Also on the agenda is a proposal to amend Article 4 of TSE Resolution No. 23.385/2012 to regulate the date of popular consultations held concurrently with municipal and general elections.

item.title: Lula sanciona MP do Frete para caminhoneiros; entenda o que muda
item.description: President Lula signed into law the MP on freight, strengthening enforcement of the minimum freight price for truckers. The new law empowers the ANTT to monitor and penalize companies violating the minimum rate, factoring in distance, operational costs, fuel prices, and cargo specifics. The Senate removed the clause setting a R$ 5,000 salary floor for long-haul transporters, leaving it to be defined by future regulation.

item.title: DC lança Clariana Barão como candidata à Presidência da República
item.description: The Christian Democracy party (DC) officially nominated Clariana Barão, a lawyer and state party president in Mato Grosso, as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections, with Fabiana Torquato as her running mate. Clariana, a mother and advocate for social causes, said she accepted the challenge to build a better Brazil and support women and children. This marks the first time since the party's founding in 1995 that its founder, José Maria Eymael, is not running for president, following rejections by Aldo Rebelo and Joaquim Barbosa.

item.title: Criticado por recuar sobre mulher como vice, Flávio diz que 'fez duas filhas' para ter quem cuide dele na velhice; vídeo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro justified choosing a man, Alfredo Gaspar, as his running mate by saying he 'had two daughters' so they could take care of him in old age, sparking criticism for reinforcing gender stereotypes. The remark came during an event where he attacked Lula’s government over the INSS scandal and announced Gaspar as his vice-presidential pick. The shift from his earlier promise to include a woman on the ticket frustrated the PL’s female wing, which had worked for months expecting a woman to join the campaign.

item.title: Efeitos da isenção de IR para a renda e para Lula começam a passar, indica nova pesquisa Quaest
item.description: The August 2026 Genial-Quaest poll shows that while a majority of beneficiaries of Lula’s IR exemption for incomes up to R$5,000 still perceive some gain (53%), the perception of improved income is declining: 46% now say the measure made no difference, up from 39% in July. The share reporting significant improvement dropped from 24% to 21%, signaling a weakening political impact of the policy.

item.title: PGR denuncia blogueiro Oswaldo Eustáquio por associação criminosa
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office denounced blogger Oswaldo Eustáquio, a Bolsonaro supporter living in exile in Spain, for criminal association based on social media posts and involvement in acts opposing Lula's 2022 inauguration. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Eustáquio to submit a preliminary defense within 15 days. Eustáquio claims political persecution and says Spain’s National Court ruled the matter as protected free speech.

item.title: g1 e GloboNews entrevistam nesta quinta-feira (6) Romeu Zema, candidato à Presidência da República
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, will be interviewed on Thursday (6) by g1 and GloboNews as the second in a series that began with Renan Santos (Missão) on Wednesday and continues with Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) on Friday. Lula declined the invitation, and Flávio Bolsonaro has not yet confirmed for the Monday (10) interview. The interview will be conducted by journalists Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM, broadcast live and simultaneously.

item.title: PSB e aliados fecham chapa majoritária de Simone Tebet em SP
item.description: The PSB has named Laio Moraes (PT) as first alternate and Marcelo Barbieri (PDT) as second alternate on Simone Tebet’s Senate ticket for São Paulo, strengthening a broad center-left front. The campaign says the composition aligns with commitments to democracy, social justice, and party unity. Meanwhile, Lula is also pushing for Marina Silva (REDE) to run in the same race, with both candidates splitting voter preference in recent polls.

item.title: Bolsa cai 0,09% com Copom no radar; dólar recua
item.description: The Ibovespa fell 0.09% and the dollar declined 0.06% as investors await the Copom decision, with expectations of a 0.25 percentage point Selic cut for the fourth consecutive time. The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 presidential race, albeit with a narrowed margin. Markets also reacted to signals of a U.S.-Iran agreement on maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, weighing on oil prices.

item.title: Tabela do frete: Lula sanciona novas regras e define obrigatoriedade de preço mínimo, mas não fixa valores
item.description: President Lula signed a law making minimum freight payments mandatory for road transport, without setting specific values, leaving updates to the ANTT based on operational costs like fuel and tolls. The law introduces the CIOT, enforces penalties for non-compliance, and removed the proposed amnesty for truckers involved in 2022 protests. The Senate rejected a proposed R$ 5,000 monthly minimum wage for long-haul truckers as unconstitutional.

item.title: Acusação de estupro, 'arma contra Lulinha' e Arthur Lira mais perto do Senado: os impactos de Alfredo Gaspar como vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The selection of Alfredo Gaspar (PL) as vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) ticket aims to exploit the INSS scandal and investigations against Lulinha to weaken the Lula government. Gaspar, who served as rapporteur of the INSS CPMI, faces a criminal complaint alleging rape of a minor, which could harm the Bolsonaro campaign. His candidacy also clears the way for Arthur Lira (PP) to pursue a Senate seat in Alagoas, as both were competing for the same right-wing electorate.

item.title: Flávio usa broche de tesoura verde e amarela em anúncio de Gaspar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro wore a green and yellow scissors brooch when announcing Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate in the PL presidential ticket, symbolizing his promised 'tesouraço' to cut taxes and bureaucracy. Gaspar was selected after other center-right options declined, with the decision reportedly made six months ago according to Valdemar Costa Neto.
